title: Contrast-Enhanced Subharmonic Aided Pressure Estimation (SHAPE) Using Ultrasound Imaging with a Focus on Identifying Portal Hypertension
protocol: Review the subject’s known drug allergies or intolerances, particularly any allergy to the UCA being used.
Exclude subjects with unstable cardiopulmonary conditions or who are generally medically unstable.
Place the subject on a stretcher in the supine position.
Insert an 18 - 22 gauge cannula into a vein in the subject’s right or left arm for the UCA infusion.
Ensure emergency services, such as a crash cart, are available within the hospital in case of acute adverse reactions.
Perforate the stopper of the UCA vial with a chemospike.
Remove the protective cap from the syringe port of the chemospike and add 2 mL of sterile water.
Shake the product for 1 minute to ensure a homogeneous product.
Withdraw the product into the syringe and re-inject the product back into the vial.
Reattach the protective cap on the chemospike.
Repeat the reconstitution procedure for the other two vials.
Use saline (0.9% NaCl solution) to fill up the connecting tubes before being connected to a 3-way stopcock.
Draw all three vials of suspended UCA into a 10 mL syringe.
Place the syringe in a syringe pump at the same level or below the patient.
Connect directly to the stopcock.
Infuse NaCl solution at a rate of 120 mL/hour.
Co-infuse Sonazoid at a rate of 0.024 µL per kg body weight per minute (suspension infusion rate of 0.18 mL/kg/hour).
Power up an ultrasound scanner and select the C1-6-D curvilinear probe.
Select an abdominal preset on the ultrasound scanner.
Acquire grayscale images of both the portal vein and a hepatic vein in the same imaging plane using a curvilinear array.
Optimize the images based on Good Clinical Practice.
Activate SHI contrast imaging mode in dual display mode.
Activate Contrast mode and select SUBH-AM on the rotary control.
Perform SHI at a transmit frequency of 2.5 MHz.
Obtain received signals at 1.25 MHz.
Use pulse-shaping to maximize the generation of subharmonic microbubble signals.
Confirm the patency of the portal and the hepatic vein as well as the presence of microbubbles.
Activate the SHAPE automated optimization code to optimize SHAPE by compensating for varying depth and attenuation.
Select TIC Analysis on the touch panel followed by F6 and then the k button.
Position an ROI on the portal vein in the contrast sample window.
Plot the average subharmonic data within the ROI as a function of acoustic output.
Fit a logistic curve to the plotted data.
Select the inflection point of the fitted curve as the optimized power.
Adjust the acoustic output power to the value identified for maximum sensitivity.
Acquire subharmonic data from the microbubbles in 5-15 s segments during the infusion of the UCA suspension.
Select “TIC Analysis” on the touch panel after acquiring the optimized SHI cine-loop.
Activate “Motion Tracking” on the touch panel to adjust ROI position for each frame.
Select dB as the unit for the Y-axis on the traces in the analysis window.
Choose identical ROIs within the hepatic and portal veins in the contrast sample window.
Average the subharmonic signal (in dB) within each vessel over all frames in a 0.5 MHz bandwidth around 1.25 MHz.
Calculate the final SHAPE gradient as the difference in mean subharmonic signal between the hepatic and portal vein ROIs.
